newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Singapore says WTO to set agenda for free trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore says WTO to set agenda for free trade.

text.p: Singapore trade and industry minister Yeo Cheow Tong said on Saturday next month's World Trade Organisation (WTO) meeting should pledge commitment to a timetable for trade liberalisation into the next century.

Yeo, who will chair the inaugural ministerial meeting of the group in Singapore, told Reuters he hoped the more than 150 WTO nations would commit to progress on issues such as labour standards, investment and transparency in government procurement.

The WTO, which succeeded the Uruguay Round of trade talks under the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) in 1994, already has an outline agenda for trade liberalisation on a range of products and services.
Yeo said he would like WTO members to commit to a strict timetable of liberalisation.
"We would like to see a firm commitment to achieving the timetable," he said at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting in Manila.
"If we are able to meet the time-frame as specified, then we would have in front of us a process for continuing trade liberalisation discussions for the next four or five years.
"We should be able to chart the whole work programme for the next few years," he said.
Yeo said it was essential WTO members stuck to their pledges to cut tariffs.
"The credibility of the whole multilateral trading process depends on all of us meeting our obligations," he said.

Yeo said he hoped the Singapore WTO meeting would be able to agree formally to a proposed Information Technology Agreement (ITA) to remove tariffs on an estimated $1.8 trillion worth of computer and other high technology products.
The proposal was criticised by Malaysia at APEC on Friday as inflexible on timing but Yeo said the United States, the leading proponent of the ITA, had indicated it was prepared to be flexible.

Yeo said he hoped a discussion over whether the question of labour standards should be raised at the WTO could be resolved before the Singapore meeting so that the ministers could get on with other areas.
Singapore did not think the WTO was the right place to discuss labour standards but would try to seek a consensus or compromise, he said.
Yeo said he hoped the WTO would also make progress on the liberalisation of telecommunications services so that a global free trade agreement could be agreed by next February.
